correctness.rationale: Gaussian STFT square completion gives a nowhere-zero prefactor times P(u)=Z0+sqrt(beta) Z1 u+Z2 u^2; omega<balanced mu is |u|<1. For a boundary-root-free quadratic, Rouché applied to conj(C)P-A P* = u[D+du] gives N=1 iff |D|>|d|. Independent complex-Gaussian orthogonalization reduces to |T|<|sqrt(beta)Z1| for T standard real normal, yielding q=E exp(-T^2/beta)=sqrt(beta/(beta+2)). Reversal symmetry gives tails (1-q)/2; two simple nonzero roots almost surely. Valid all beta>0, no finite Monte Carlo used as proof.
